report:
Reviewed the complete fixed_projection claim, all three ordinary implementation associations (rust_ref shared schema, sage_emit::emit_module, and sage_oracle::emit::emit_crate), and the sole associated TODO test. Added the schema association and restarted the review so changes to the vocabulary itself invalidate this assessment.

The fixed/native-only projection requirement is satisfied at the adapter boundary: Sage accepts only its Db and ModSymbol, and its Emitter stores that database plus its own definition map/counter. The rustc adapter accepts only TyCtxt, checks compiler errors, and stores that context plus its own definition map/counter. Neither receives or reads the opposite emitted value. Both independently pre-register local definitions, translate constructors to their owning definition, and translate external paths and native definition kinds. The kind conversion functions reject unrepresentable kinds rather than intentionally turning them into a common namespace label. These are fixed native identity translations, not decisions made from a pair of outputs.

The permitted adjustment and lifetime qualifications are explicit in the implementation. Sage emits its elaborated ResolvedCall, Ref, Deref and NeverToAny nodes directly. Rustc translates native receiver/call adjustments, retains mutability and adjustment target types, and synthesizes primitive overloadable operators from the corresponding language-item method and native operand types. Lazy boolean operators remain BinaryOp. Unsupported receiver adjustments panic rather than disappearing to match Sage. Resolved method/operator calls preserve dispatch, Self/trait substitutions, owner arguments, method arguments and argument order. Both type adapters intentionally omit reference regions while retaining referent types and mutability; the shared Type::Ref has no region field, matching the claim's explicitly deferred lifetime representation.

The schema association accounts for the vocabulary requirement: rust-ref represents definition kinds, alias kinds and inputs, dispatch and substitutions, field owner/index, and explicit borrow/deref/coercion nodes. Both adapters construct these same variants independently. In particular the alias cases preserve named/associated/opaque classification and ordered inputs, rather than erasing an alias because its counterpart differs. Schema evolution must change that vocabulary and both producers; this review makes no claim that every future Rust construct is represented already. The recorded oracle guide explicitly separates supported slice coverage from the still-developing general coverage boundary. Existing fixed unsupported sentinels, unsupported item omissions, and empty variant-field representations are limitations of that frontier, not evidence of pair-dependent output repair; they do not establish conformance or coverage and are not approved here as such. The independent_coverage anchor governs acceptance of such outputs.

Test adequacy remains explicitly TODO. The only associated test, sage_meta::todo::crates_sage_oracle_harness_crate_fixed_projection, has no behavioral assertions. Its comment specifically defers associating and reviewing the complete adapter matrix: native definition kinds, substitutions, receiver adjustments, operator calls, lifetimes and unsupported constructs, plus independent omission/wrong-classification adversarial cases. This is an accepted existing evidence deferral, not a passing behavioral test. Completing that matrix and attaching inspectable assertions is the prerequisite for replacing the TODO; neither this review nor the schema unit tests discharge it. No N/A entries or implementation TODOs are present.

Source inspection covered the complete captured adapter/schema files and recorded design/review context. The historical oracle RFD is explicitly superseded where it proposes paired normalization; the current claim and oracle guide supply the assessed contract. Executed cargo fmt, cargo test -p rust-ref (seven unit tests passed; zero doc tests), and cargo build (passed with existing warnings). Those commands verify the comment-only association edit/build, not the deferred adapter matrix. No behavioral reproduction or full oracle conformance run is claimed. Centralized delegated post-codegen and Sage sanity checks are coordinated by root for this one-comment edit.
